issues.failure_explanation: The example asserts that the multi-asset Black–Scholes model satisfies Assumptions 2.1 and 2.5. But Assumption 2.1(ii) and 2.5(i) demand uniform ellipticity on all of [0,T]×R^d with a fixed κ>0, while σ(x)=σ diag(x) degenerates whenever some coordinate x^i=0 (and its eigenvalues are not bounded below anywhere). The same model is used in Section 5, so neither the worked example nor the numerical experiments fall under the paper's stated hypotheses (which are used in Theorems 2.3, 2.4 and the viscosity arguments of Section 3).

failure_location.quote: Then, it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde} hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the example in log-coordinates (dynamics with constant σ, payoffs composed with exp, which remain Lipschitz) or restrict the state space to the positive orthant with appropriate localisation, and state this explicitly for the experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The only example and the numerical study are formally outside the scope of the theory; the claim that the assumptions are 'straightforward' to verify is false as written.
issues.title: Black–Scholes example (and numerical model) violates the uniform ellipticity assumption it is claimed to satisfy
issues.why_classification: A standard change of variables restores the hypotheses without changing any result or rate; the defect is a false verification claim rather than a flaw in the theory.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying Ekeland's variational principle \citep{Ekeland1974} to the continuous function \(-\ell\) on the complete metric space \(K\)

issues.failure_explanation: Counterexample satisfying Assumptions 2.1, 2.5, 3.1: d=1, b=0, σ=1, f≡0, p_b(t,x)=g(x)=-|x|, p_w≡1, X_0≠0. Then D_b=inf 𝓛p_b=0 off Γ={0}, so the proposition claims V^λ≥p_b everywhere. But if V^λ≥-|x| then f_λ(V^λ)=-λ(1-V^λ)^-≤0, whence V^λ(t,x)=E[-|x+W_{T-t}|+∫f_λ]<-|x| for t<T (strict Jensen), a contradiction. Quantitatively the stationary reduced equation ½u''+λu^-=δ_0 gives λ(V^λ-p_b)^-(0)≈√(λ/2)→∞, i.e. the classical λ^{-1/2} rate is sharp for concave kinks of the lower barrier, which Assumption 3.1(ii) permits (it bounds only |[∂_n p]|, not its sign). In the proof, the viscosity supersolution inequality (eq:viscsuper) is written with the wrong sign (compare the correct convention used in (T5:1)); with the correct sign Case 1 still closes, but in Case 2 the perturbation contributes +𝓛ρ_η(t_η,x_η)=(η/δ)tr(σσ^T)>0 to the upper bound, and since δ<dist(x̄,Γ) can be forced to be O(η) when the maximum sits on a kink, this term does not vanish as η→0. Additionally Ekeland's principle yields a distance (non-smooth) perturbation, not the squared-distance one used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a sign condition on the kinks ([∂_{n_k}p_b]≥0 and [∂_{n_k}p_w]≤0, i.e. the singular parts of 𝓛p_b, 𝓛p_w have the favourable sign), correct the sign of the supersolution inequality, and rewrite Case 2 with an argument that handles maxima on Γ (e.g. via one-sided semijets), noting that the paper's own basket-put example then only qualifies on the positive orthant.
issues.overall_effect: The headline improved penalization rate O(λ^{-1}) (Theorem 3.5, Corollary 3.4, Theorem 3.6) is false under the stated assumptions; all λ-uniform a priori bounds that invoke Corollary 3.4 (Prop. 4.1, Cor. 4.3) and every error bound and tuning rule built on the 1/λ term (Thm 4.4, Cor 4.6, Thm 4.5, Cor 4.7, Remark 4.8, the advertised O(Δt^{1/2}) rate) lose their proofs; with the true λ^{-1/2} penalty rate the balanced rate degrades.
issues.title: Proposition 3.3 (uniform λ^{-1} barrier-violation bound) is false under the stated assumptions; Case 2 of its proof is invalid
issues.why_classification: The primary claim is false as stated (explicit counterexample), the advertised scope (arbitrary bounded kinks) must be excluded, and a new argument for the singular set is required; the central rate results of the paper depend on it.

We compare our penalized implicit discretization, implemented with LSMC regression for conditional expectations

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (scheme) asserts 𝓨_{t_{i+1}}=𝓨_{t_i}-f_λ(...)Δt+𝓩_{t_i}ΔW_{i+1} as an exact identity with F_{t_i}-measurable 𝓨_{t_i},𝓩_{t_i}. Since 𝓨_{t_n}=g(X^{π̃}_{t_n}) is a nonlinear functional of the m fine Brownian increments on (t_{n-1},t_n], it is in general not affine in ΔW_n, so no such triple exists; the actual (implemented) scheme is (discretization), for which (scheme) holds only up to a martingale increment ΔM orthogonal to ΔW. The proof of Theorem 4.4 squares (final1) and uses Itô isometry, which requires the exact identity; with the extra ΔM the left-hand side changes and the term E∫|Z^λ_s-𝓩_{t_i}|^2 is no longer controlled without an L^2-regularity estimate for Z^λ (with λ-dependence tracked). Theorem 4.5 is not affected because its proof only uses conditional expectations, under which ΔM vanishes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Theorems 4.4/4.5 for (discretization); in the proof of Theorem 4.4 replace the exact identity by the Bouchard–Touzi/Zhang argument with the orthogonal martingale increment and supply an L^2-regularity bound for Z^λ with explicit λ-dependence, adjusting the constant/rate accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.4 and Corollary 4.6 (the general Lipschitz, Z-dependent mean-square bounds and the O(Δt^{1/4}) rate claimed in the introduction) are not established for the scheme that is actually defined and implemented; Corollary 4.7 also formally applies Theorem 4.5 outside its stated hypothesis, though its proof carries over.
issues.title: L^2 error theorem is proved for the exact forward identity (scheme), which the implemented implicit scheme (discretization) does not satisfy
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial additional argument (λ-dependent Z-regularity) is needed and the resulting constant may worsen, but no new global architecture is required and the Z-independent results survive.
